# Benchmarks

```{r model_family_header, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
acousticTS:::.model_family_header(
  family = "pcdwba",
  pages = c(
    Overview = "index.html",
    Theory = "pcdwba-theory.html",
    Implementation = "pcdwba-implementation.html",
    Benchmarks = "pcdwba-benchmarks.html",
    Validation = "pcdwba-validation.html"
  )
)
```

The current PCDWBA benchmark case is a curved, weakly scattering cylinder evaluated from `12-200 kHz` in `2 kHz` steps with `51` integration nodes. The geometry is length `15 mm`, radius `1 mm`, taper order `10`, curvature ratio `rho_c / L = 3`, density contrast `g = 1.02`, sound-speed contrast `h = 1.02`, and broadside incidence.

| Benchmark comparison | Max abs. $\Delta TS$ (dB) | Mean abs. $\Delta TS$ (dB) |
|:--|--:|--:|
| acousticTS vs `ZooScatR` | 9.95e-13 | 1.05e-14 |
| acousticTS vs `Echopop` | 0.07395 | 0.00112 |
| `Echopop` vs `ZooScatR` | 0.07395 | 0.00112 |

| Evaluation path | Elapsed (s) | Frequency range (kHz) | Frequency step (kHz) | Node count |
|:--|--:|:--|--:|--:|
| acousticTS | 0.01 | `12-200` | 2 | 51 |
| `ZooScatR` | 0.12 | `12-200` | 2 | 51 |
| `Echopop` | 3.31 | `12-200` | 2 | 51 |

::: {.note data-title="Why this is the benchmark case"}
PCDWBA is a curved-body model, so the benchmark should retain curvature. A straight-body reduction is useful as a diagnostic, but it is not the benchmark target for this public model surface.
:::
